lessons.title: Phone basics: moving around with TalkBack
steps: Welcome. In this lesson you will learn to move around your phone with TalkBack, the screen reader built into Android. Take your time. You can pause at any point.
When TalkBack is on, touching the screen does not press anything. It reads out what is under your finger. Slide one finger slowly around the screen and listen.
To move to the next item, swipe right with one finger. To go back to the item before, swipe left. Each item is read as you reach it.
To press the item TalkBack has just read, double tap anywhere on the screen: two quick taps with one finger.
To scroll a long page, swipe up or down with two fingers.
Practise now: on Magana's home screen, swipe right until you hear Read a page. Then double tap to open it.

lessons.title: Taking clear photos of pages
steps: In this lesson you will learn to take a clear photo of a printed page, so Magana can read it well.
Find good light. Daylight near a window is best. A torch shone straight at shiny paper causes glare, so light the page from the side.
Lay the page flat on a table. Hold the phone flat above it, with the camera facing down, about thirty centimetres away. That is about the length from your elbow to your wrist.
Magana tells you which way to move the phone, with short words and a tone. When the whole page fits, hold still and take the photo.
If Magana says the text is faint or blurred, add more light, hold the phone steadier, and take the photo again.
Practise now: open Read a page and photograph any printed page near you.

lessons.title: Money: reading a bank statement safely
steps: In this lesson you will learn to read a bank statement or a receipt with Magana, safely.
Open Everyday papers, then Bank statement. Take the photo as you learned in the photo lesson.
Magana reads tables row by row: the date, the description, then the amount. Numbers and amounts are read exactly as printed. If a number is unclear, Magana says so instead of guessing.
Magana never asks for your PIN or password, and nobody from Magana ever will. Do not say your PIN aloud near other people, and never share it on a call.
Magana does not give financial advice. If something on your statement looks wrong, call your bank on the number printed on your card.
Practise now: read a receipt or statement from Everyday papers.
